extracted.intended_audience: students and teachers of classical Euclidean geometry
extracted.subtask_description: Extracts and states the principal propositions and constructive theorems from Book I of Euclid's Elements (propositions XVI–XLI plus nearby corollaries and constructions). These are rules/theorems about triangles, angles, parallel lines, parallelograms, and constructions used to produce or reason about plane geometry figures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Angles about intersection sum to four right angles (Cor. 1)
rubrics_metrics.description: If two straight lines cut one another, the angles they make at the point where they cut are together equal to four right angles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Immediate corollary of earlier proposition: take the four angles created at the intersection; they sum to four right angles. (Used as a basic algebraic/angle accounting fact in subsequent proofs.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Angles formed by many lines at a point sum to four right angles (Cor. 2)
rubrics_metrics.description: All the angles made by any number of lines meeting in one point are together equal to four right angles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Generalisation of the previous corollary: partition into pairs or use induction by adding one line at a time. Useful for reasoning about multiple rays from a point.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exterior angle greater than either interior opposite angle (Prop. XVI)
rubrics_metrics.description: If one side of a triangle be produced, the exterior angle is greater than either of the interior opposite angles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construction in proof: bisect the opposite side, join and extend to create an isosceles comparison; use vertical angles and equality of sides to deduce base equality and compare angles. This is a fundamental inequality about triangle angles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Any two angles of a triangle less than two right angles (Prop. XVII)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any two angles of a triangle are together less than two right angles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof uses producing a side to form an exterior angle which is greater than an interior opposite angle, then adds the remaining triangle angle and compares to two right angles. Foundational for angle-sum reasoning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Greater side opposite the greater angle (Prop. XVIII)
rubrics_metrics.description: The greater side of every triangle is opposite to the greater angle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Given a triangle with one side longer than another, mark off an equal segment and apply the exterior-angle inequality to compare opposite angles. Provides monotonic relation between side length and opposite angle.

rubrics_metrics.name: Greater angle subtends greater side (Prop. XIX)
rubrics_metrics.description: The greater angle of every triangle is subtended by the greater side, or has the greater side opposite to it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contrapositive/reciprocal of Prop. XVIII: if an angle is greater than another, show the opposite side must be greater by ruling out equality or being less via contradiction. Used in side-angle-side comparisons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sum of any two sides greater than third (Triangle inequality) (Prop. XX)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any two sides of a triangle are together greater than the third side.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct on a produced side a segment equal to the third side; use triangle angle inequalities to show the constructed side plus original side exceeds the remaining side. Fundamental metric inequality in triangle geometry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two lines from ends to internal point shorter than opposite sides but form larger angle (Prop. XXI)
rubrics_metrics.description: If, from the ends of the side of a triangle, there be drawn two straight lines to a point within the triangle, these shall be less than the other two sides of the triangle, but shall contain a greater angle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof uses triangle inequality applied to external constructions and compares exterior and interior opposite angles to establish both length and angle relations. Useful when dealing with internal points and chord-like segments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construct triangle with three given sides if any two greater than third (Prop. XXII, Problem)
rubrics_metrics.description: To make a triangle of which the sides shall be equal to three given straight lines, provided any two of these are greater than the third.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construction: lay the three segments consecutively on a line, draw circles with appropriate radii from endpoints to find third vertex (intersection of circles), then join to form triangle. Includes existence condition (triangle inequality) explicitly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construct at given point on line an angle equal to a given angle (Prop. XXIII, Problem)
rubrics_metrics.description: At a given point in a given straight line, to make a rectilineal angle equal to a given rectilineal angle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construction reduces to constructing a triangle with sides equal to chosen segments from the given angle and transferring that triangle to the line and point, thereby creating an equal angle. Demonstrates method of angle copy via triangle congruence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Base opposite greater included angle is greater (Prop. XXIV)
rubrics_metrics.description: If two triangles have two sides of one equal to two sides of the other, each to each, but the angle contained by the two sides of one is greater than the angle contained by the two sides of the other, the base of that which has the greater angle shall be greater than the base of the other.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct auxiliary equal segments and apply previous angle-side relations to compare bases. Useful for comparing triangles with two equal sides and differing included angles.

rubrics_metrics.name: If equal sides but larger base, included angle larger (Prop. XXV)
rubrics_metrics.description: If two triangles have two sides of the one equal to two sides of the other, each to each, but the base of the one greater than the base of the other; the angle also contained by the sides of that which has the greater base shall be greater than the angle contained by the sides equal to them, of the other.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Essential converse to Prop. XXIV: uses contradiction to rule out equality or less-than, and relies on previous equality/inequality results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Triangles with two angles and one side equal are congruent (Prop. XXVI)
rubrics_metrics.description: If two triangles have two angles of one equal to two angles of the other, each to each; and one side equal to one side (either adjacent to equal angles or opposite to equal angles in each), then the other sides shall be equal each to each, and the third angles equal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two cases covered: equal adjacent sides or equal opposite sides. Proofs use construction to create equal triangles and contradiction to force equalities. This is angle-angle-side congruence variant and provides triangle congruence conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternate interior angles equal implies lines parallel (Prop. XXVII)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a straight line falling upon two other straight lines makes the alternate angles equal to one another, these two straight lines shall be parallel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof by contradiction: assume they meet; then an exterior/interior angle inequality contradicts the equality. This gives a criterion to assert parallelism from angle equality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exterior interior-equality or interior sum two right angles implies parallel (Prop. XXVIII)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a straight line falling upon two other straight lines makes the exterior angle equal to the interior and opposite upon the same side of the line; or makes the interior angles upon the same side together equal to two right angles; the two straight lines shall be parallel to one another.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shows alternate formulations equivalent to Prop. XXVII: equality between certain angles or sum being two right angles are both sufficient to deduce parallelism. Useful for different angle relations when testing parallel lines.

rubrics_metrics.name: If line falls on parallel lines then alternate/interior relations hold (Prop. XXIX)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a straight line fall upon two parallel straight lines, it makes the alternate angles equal to one another; and the exterior angle equal to the interior and opposite upon the same side; and likewise the two interior angles upon the same side together equal to two right angles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Converse of previous: given parallelism deduce angle equalities and sums. Used extensively to translate between parallelism and angle conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lines parallel to the same line are parallel to one another (Prop. XXX)
rubrics_metrics.description: Straight lines which are parallel to the same straight line are parallel to one another.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof uses a transversal and equality of corresponding/alternate angles to deduce parallelism by Prop. XXVII/XXIX. Fundamental transitivity property of parallelism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construct through a point a line parallel to a given line (Prop. XXXI, Problem)
rubrics_metrics.description: To draw a straight line through a given point parallel to a given straight line.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construction: pick an arbitrary point on the given line, join it to the given point, copy corresponding alternate angle at the given point, and extend. Uses angle-copying construction (Prop. XXIII) and Prop. XXVII to conclude parallelism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exterior angle equals sum of two interior opposite; triangle angles sum two right angles (Prop. XXXII)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a side of any triangle be produced, the exterior angle is equal to the two interior and opposite angles; and the three interior angles of every triangle are equal to two right angles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof uses drawing through vertex a line parallel to opposite side to produce equal alternate angles, then equates exterior to sum of two interior angles and hence total of three interior equals two right angles. Core result for angle-sum of triangle and polygon corollaries that follow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interior angles of rectilineal figure plus four right angles equals twice number of sides right angles (Cor. 1 to Prop. XXXII)
rubrics_metrics.description: All the interior angles of any rectilineal figure, together with four right angles, are equal to twice as many right angles as the figure has sides.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Divide polygon into triangles from an interior point; sum triangle angle sums to deduce polygon angle-sum formula. Gives polygon interior-angle sum in terms of number of sides.

rubrics_metrics.name: All exterior angles of rectilineal figure sum to four right angles (Cor. 2 to Prop. XXXII)
rubrics_metrics.description: All the exterior angles of any rectilineal figure are together equal to four right angles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because interior+adjacent exterior = two right angles, summing over polygon yields exterior sum = four right angles. Useful for turning-turn/path-angle interpretations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lines joining ends of equal & parallel segments are equal and parallel (Prop. XXXIII)
rubrics_metrics.description: The straight lines which join the extremities of two equal and parallel straight lines, towards the same parts, are also themselves equal and parallel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof compares triangles formed and uses alternate angles with side equalities to deduce equality and parallelism. Helps build parallelogram/parallel-shift arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opposite sides and angles of parallelogram equal; diagonal bisects (Prop. XXXIV)
rubrics_metrics.description: The opposite sides and angles of parallelograms are equal to one another, and the diameter (diagonal) bisects them (divides them into two equal parts).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uses triangle congruence on halves formed by diagonal and parallel properties. Also includes NB defining parallelogram and diameter. Fundamental parallelogram properties used throughout geometry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parallelograms on same base & between same parallels are equal (Prop. XXXV)
rubrics_metrics.description: Parallelograms upon the same base, and between the same parallels, are equal to one another.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Argues by partition into triangles or by translating one parallelogram to coincide partly; reduction to equality of triangles leads to equality of parallelogram areas (Euclid's notion of 'equal' figures).

rubrics_metrics.name: Parallelograms on equal bases between same parallels are equal (Prop. XXXVI)
rubrics_metrics.description: Parallelograms upon equal bases, and between the same parallels, are equal to one another.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Join corresponding vertices to form intermediate parallelogram and use earlier proposition about joining equal & parallel lines to transfer equality; another area-equality statement (Euclid's equal-figure reasoning).

rubrics_metrics.name: Triangles on same base & between same parallels equal (Prop. XXXVII)
rubrics_metrics.description: Triangles upon the same base, and between the same parallels, are equal to one another.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reduce to parallelogram-halves: extend to parallelograms, note each triangle is half of a parallelogram, apply equality of parallelograms and halves-of-equal-things principle.

rubrics_metrics.name: Triangles on equal bases between same parallels equal (Prop. XXXVIII)
rubrics_metrics.description: Triangles upon equal bases, and between the same parallels, are equal to one another.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Similar to Prop. XXXVII but bases equal rather than same; extend to parallelograms and deduce equality via halves of equal parallelograms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equal triangles on same base & same side lie between same parallels (Prop. XXXIX)
rubrics_metrics.description: Equal triangles upon the same base, and upon the same side of it, are between the same parallels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If two triangles on the same base are equal, the line joining their vertices must be parallel to the base; otherwise contradiction via constructing another equal triangle on same base yields impossibility. Used to deduce position-related parallelism from area equality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equal triangles on equal bases in same line and same parts are between same parallels (Prop. XL)
rubrics_metrics.description: Equal triangles upon equal bases, in the same straight line, and towards the same parts, are between the same parallels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Argument by contradiction using constructing a parallel and comparing triangles; ensures uniqueness of the parallel that makes triangles between the same parallels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parallelogram on same base and between same parallels is double the triangle (Prop. XLI)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a parallelogram and triangle be upon the same base, and between the same parallels; the parallelogram shall be double of the triangle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Join the diagonal to show parallelogram is composed of two equal triangles (diagonal bisects parallelogram), hence parallelogram area equals twice the triangle's area. Provides Euclid's relation between parallelogram and triangle on same base/height.
